text:
A: Alright.
B: Hiya. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah. I'm Ryan. Castleford.
B: Shazia. Walsall.
A: Right.
B: ...
A: Erm. What do you do then?
B: I'm at home. Housewife, I suppose. Three kids. I used to work at a warehouse, packing, but me back went. You?
A: Mechanic. Garage near Normanton.
B: Oh, right. My husband drives a taxi. Private hire. His car's always got something wrong with it, to be honest.
A: What's he drive?
B: Erm, a Toyota. The hybrid one, the Prius. Silver.
A: Them are good, to be fair. Most taxi drivers have 'em. What's up with it?
B: There's some light on the dashboard. And it makes this noise when he brakes, like a grinding. He took it to a place on the Wednesbury Road and they wanted four hundred quid and they didn't even tell him what it was properly. Just "it's the brakes, mate". And he needs that car, d'you know what I mean, if it's off the road we've got nothing coming in that week. So I wasn't happy.
A: Grinding's probably pads worn down to the metal. Then it's chewed the discs. On a Prius the brakes go regenerative a lot of the time so they last longer, but taxi mileage, they'll still go. Four hundred for discs and pads all round's not daylight robbery, but they should've shown him. I always show people the old parts.
B: See, that's all he wanted. Just tell him.
A: Light could be owt though. Needs plugging in.
B: Okay. I'll tell him that.
A: Yeah.
B: ...
A: Did you do that puzzle at the start?
B: Yeah. Didn't get far. Is this what we're doing, just chatting?
A: Think so.
B: Do you know if we get paid at the end or after?
A: Dunno. After, I think.
B: Right. It better come through. I've done ones before where it never came.
A: Fair.
B: Have you got kids?
A: No. Just a dog. Me and me girlfriend.
B: Enjoy it while you can. My youngest won't walk to school, so I'm driving him in the rain every morning, and the middle one's glued to his PlayStation.
A: I'm on the PlayStation most nights an' all, to be fair.
B: How old are you?
A: Twenty-seven.
B: You've got no excuse then.
A: Ha. No.
B: My eldest is doing her A-levels. She wants to go uni. Manchester, maybe. I'm proud of her, but I don't want her that far, d'you know what I mean.
A: Manchester's not that far.
B: It is when you've never been away from your mum.
A: Suppose. My sister went to Leeds. Me mam cried for a week.
B: There you go.
A: She's fine now though.
